item.title: Re: On the topic of the criminals plan
item.content:encoded:
I don't understand why this is the hill you both seem to want to die on.

You mean it annoys you when my behavior doesn't make sense?

ahem

Because you've repeatedly shown you're capable of much better than this. And in fact, this is a pretty good SCP in all other ways - conceptually, the anomaly is easy to grasp, and the experiment log is perfect (if a bit discomfiting).

Dado him/her/it/themself is a great concept - I'd started tinkering with the notion of the Foundation having an anomalous drugmaker in custody a few years ago, but couldn't make it work. Of course it's better if we only have the products, not the producer. And the personality revealed in those chat logs is gold. There's tons of potential here; there'll be a dado tag soon, and dado tales. Other pre-existing pharma-based SCPs (not SCP-500, though) might even be retconned into dadowork, the way that pre-existing toylike SCPs were retconned into being wondertainment.

Ultimately, this SCP is powered by the characters' stupidity. It's a question of how much stupidity one can tolerate.

It's just one dumb article about a dude selling boner pills

Don't put yourself down. Aside from that one plot hole which I can't not see, this is a decent little article, and you should feel good about it.

I know you care about this project — about having the tales and articles be as high-quality as possible. I've listened to your podcasts, I've read your proposed remake of 049. I care about this project too. That's why I fuss about all the details. But there's a stopping point — even though I'm sure my version of SCP-166 would be better than what we have, I've long since let that one go.

This is my final statement pertaining to SCP-3929.

item.content:encoded: Looking pretty good. This one cracked me up. I did notice one thing, though. "SCP-3929 is the group designation for a supply of roughly one-hundred twenty seven dark umber pharmaceutical capsules…" 127 doesn't seem to be the kind of number where they wouldn't want to obtain an exact count. The research team responsible for writing up the article would likely include at least one person trained in pharmacology, possibly even with prior experience working at a mundane pharmacy. That person would definitely want to obtain an exact count rather than leave it at "roughly" 127 pills. Now, if it was a crate full of pill bottles that would be a different story altogether. But 127 pills can fit in one to five bottles, depending on the size. Easy count.
